paragraphs: Rabbi Yehoshua, son of Rabbi Timi.

In Kohelet Rabbah, at the supplied locator פ״טו [compare 9:9:1], Rabbi Yitzchak ben Elazar called Rabbi Yehoshua, son of Rabbi Timi, and Rabbi Burki the holy congregation. It appears to Hyman that one should read R' Hoshaya, son of R' Shammai.

notes.text: The printed Kohelet Rabbah locator פ״טו remains unresolved. The source does not explicitly state which of the two named men is to be corrected to Hoshaya son of Shammai; the earlier model’s preference for Burki is not adopted.

The saved whole ToratEmet KoheletRabbah9:9:1 scalar really contains two holy-congregation pairs: after Yose ben Meshullam and Shimon ben Menasya, Rabbi Yitzchak ben Elazar names Rabbi Yehoshua son of Rabbi Timei and Rabbi Burkei. The earlier categorical nonmatch is superseded for this actual text. Supplied פ״טו stays beside9:9:1 without a printed-glyph claim. Hyman’s it appears one should read Hoshaya son of Shammai remains tentative and is not validated by the Yehoshua passage. The proposed names’ abbreviated titles stay R'.

Hyman’s printed notice on p. 635 gives the short locator reproduced in the Hebrew. Kohelet Rabbah 9:9:1 calls both pairs a holy congregation: first Yose ben Meshullam and Shimon ben Menasya, and then Yehoshua son of Timi and Burki in Rabbi Yitzchak ben Elazar’s account. The latter pair divided their time among Torah, prayer, and work. The passage leaves Hyman’s suggested reading of Hoshaya son of Shammai unconfirmed.
